Validate a completed coding sheet against the model

validate_sample.Rd

Takes the sheet coding_sample() wrote, with human_label filled in, and reports how well the model agreed with the coder.

The sheet carries no probabilities, which is what makes it blind. This joins back to the results on id and item to recover them, so pass the same results object the sample came from.

vignette("complete_run") works a run end to end.

Usage

validate_sample(
  sheet,
  results,
  ...,
  level = c("nominal", "ordinal"),
  labels = NULL,
  instrument = NULL,
  calibration = FALSE,
  coded = FALSE,
  ci = c("none", "bootstrap"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  bootstrap_n = 2000L,
  seed = 1234L
)

Arguments

sheet

A data frame holding the completed coding sheet, or a string giving a path to the CSV. A named list of sheets scores the model against every coder in it and adds the ceiling and the gap. See the section below.

results

A fathom_results object, the one the sheet was drawn from.

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

level

A string, "nominal" (the default) or "ordinal". It decides how a disagreement is charged, so it selects the proper scoring rule in $calibration as well as the alpha.

labels

A character vector giving, under "ordinal", every label in scale order. Ignored under "nominal". Default is NULL.

instrument

A fathom_instrument, the one the run used. Under "ordinal" its scores supply the scale, so labels need not be retyped. An explicit labels wins over it. Default is NULL.

calibration

A logical value indicating whether to return $calibration, for a run keeping prob_renorm and feeding it onward. Default is FALSE.

coded

A logical value indicating whether to return $coded, the sheet joined to the model's answer. Default is FALSE.

ci

A string choosing whether to report intervals. "none", the default, returns none and the interval columns are absent rather than present and full of NA. "bootstrap" adds one bracketed column beside each figure.

conf_level

A number giving the coverage of every interval reported, 0.95 by default. It is stamped on the result as the conf_level attribute, and the print method states it under the first table that carries an interval.

bootstrap_n

An integer giving the replicates for each interval. The default is a round two thousand. Below a hundred a percentile interval is reading a tail made of a handful of draws, and is refused.

seed

An integer giving the seed for the bootstrap, so the intervals come out the same on every run with the same inputs. The session's random stream is put back on exit, so nothing drawn before this call reaches the intervals and this seed reaches nothing after it. NULL draws from the session's stream instead. Default is 1234.

Value

An object of class fathom_validation, a list of tables. The model tables carry item and, on the several-sheet path, coder. Under ci = "bootstrap" each figure gains a bracketed _ci column beside it.

componentholdswhen
$discriminationhow often the model chose the coder's labela label sheet
$categoriesprecision, recall and AUC for each labela label sheet
$calibrationhow honest the probabilities werecalibration = TRUE, or a soft sheet
$ceilinghow well the coders agreed with each otherseveral sheets
$gapthe model against that ceilingseveral sheets
$codedthe sheet joined to the model's answercoded = TRUE

Discrimination

One row per question, plus a pooled (all items) row where the instrument has more than one.

  • n counts the coded rows.

  • agreement is the share of rows where the model chose the coder's label.

  • alpha is Krippendorff's alpha (Hayes and Krippendorff 2007) between the model and the coder, under the level asked for.

Categories

One row per label per question, with label and n, the rows the coder gave that label.

  • precision is the share of the rows the model gave the label where the coder chose it too.

  • recall is the share of the rows the coder gave the label where the model chose it too.

  • auc is the chance that a row the coder gave the label gets a higher probability for it than a row the coder did not.

All three count exact matches, so under "ordinal" a model one level off is charged as a full miss. alpha and rps are the figures that respect the order. On two labels the two auc rows are equal, since one label's probability is one minus the other's.

Calibration

One row per question, plus the pooled row, with n and one score column named for the rule level selects.

  • brier is squared error summed across categories, so on two labels a confident correct answer costs 0, a confident wrong one costs 2, and never committing costs 0.5.

  • rps is the same sum on the cumulative probabilities and runs from 0 to k - 1. Lower is better for both. A soft reference stays on brier.

Ceiling

$ceiling$alpha is one row per question with n_units, the rows two or more coders reached, and alpha over all coders at once. $ceiling$pairs is one row per pair of coders per question, with coder_a, coder_b, n, the rows both coded, agreement and alpha. This is what the coders managed on these rows, and not a target.

Gap

One row per question.

  • n counts the rows the model and the coders share.

  • model_alpha is the model's average alpha with the coders.

  • coder_alpha is the coders' average alpha with each other on the same rows.

  • gap is the first minus the second, positive where the model agreed with the coders more closely than they agreed with each other, and gap_ci is its interval.

Coded

The sheet joined to the model's label and its probabilities, one row per coded document-item, or per document-item per coder on the several-sheet path. It is returned because a design-based correction takes it as input (Egami et al. 2023, Angelopoulos et al. 2023).

The attributes carry level, conf_level, the number of coded rows as n_coded, and on the several-sheet path the coder names as coders.

Several coders

sheet takes a named list as well as one sheet, so validate_sample(list(ana = ana, luis = luis), res) scores the model against each coder in one call and adds $ceiling and $gap. Each coder is scored through the one-sheet path, so no figure is computed twice or computed differently, and the model tables gain a coder column after item.

Coders need not have worked every row. $ceiling$alpha uses every row two or more coders reached, and each pair in $ceiling$pairs falls back to the rows both of them saw, so the two tables can rest on different counts.

$gap resamples whatever ci is set to, since the gap is read through its interval. Every replicate redraws the documents once and recomputes both sides on that draw, because the two share the documents they rest on.

A list of one is refused. A sheet coder_reference() consolidated warns when it is placed in a list, since agreeing with a consensus is easier than agreeing with one person.

Ordered labels

Ordered labels need level = "ordinal". The default charges every disagreement the same, which is right for unordered labels and wrong for a scale, where two coders one step apart have agreed more than two coders at opposite ends. Pass labels in scale order, least to greatest, or an instrument carrying scores. Nothing is inferred, because no order can be recovered from the sheets.

A soft reference

A sheet carrying human_prop instead of human_label is scored as a measurement and not as a classification. There is no second categorical variable, so $discrimination and $categories are not returned. What comes back is $calibration, with brier against the proportion, whatever calibration is set to.

References

Angelopoulos, A. N., Bates, S., Fannjiang, C., Jordan, M. I., and Zrnic, T. (2023). Prediction-powered inference. Science 382(6671), 669–674. doi:10.1126/science.adi6000

Brier, G. W. (1950). Verification of forecasts expressed in terms of probability. Monthly Weather Review 78(1), 1–3. doi:10.1175/1520-0493(1950)078<0001:VOFEIT>2.0.CO;2

Egami, N., Hinck, M., Stewart, B., and Wei, H. (2023). Using imperfect surrogates for downstream inference. Design-based supervised learning for social science applications of large language models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36, 68589–68601. doi:10.52202/075280-3000

Hayes, A. F., and Krippendorff, K. (2007). Answering the call for a standard reliability measure for coding data. Communication Methods and Measures 1(1), 77–89. doi:10.1080/19312450709336664

See also

coding_sample() for drawing the sheet, and coder_reference() for consolidating several coders into one sheet.

Examples

# Results from a real run ship with the package, so this needs no server.
p <- system.file("extdata", "vignette_results.rds", package = "fathom")
baked <- readRDS(p)
res <- baked$res_six
sheet <- coding_sample(res, parlasent, text = "sentence", id = "id", n = 20,
  seed = 1234)
#> Blinded coding sample
#> 
#> Pairs         20 across 1 item
#> Drawn         20 of 100
#> 
#> Tip      Pass the completed sheet to validate_sample() together with these
#>          results.

# The parlasent coders, standing in for someone filling the sheet in.
six <- c("Negative", "M_Negative", "N_Neutral", "P_Neutral", "M_Positive",
  "Positive")
coded <- function(who) {
  out <- sheet
  out$human_label <- as.character(
    match(parlasent[[who]][match(sheet$id, parlasent$id)], six)
  )
  out
}
a1 <- coded("annotator1")

v <- validate_sample(a1, res, level = "ordinal", labels = as.character(1:6))
v$discrimination
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   item         n agreement alpha
#>   <chr>    <int>     <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 category    20      0.65 0.753
v$categories
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   item     label     n precision recall   auc
#>   <chr>    <chr> <int>     <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 category 1         6     1      0.667 0.887
#> 2 category 2         1     1      1     1    
#> 3 category 3         5     0.75   0.6   0.933
#> 4 category 4         1     0      0     0.842
#> 5 category 5         4     0.667  0.5   0.781
#> 6 category 6         3     0.6    1     0.980

# A second coder adds the ceiling the two set between themselves, and the
# model against it.
a2 <- coded("annotator2")
v2 <- validate_sample(list(annotator1 = a1, annotator2 = a2), res,
  level = "ordinal", labels = as.character(1:6), bootstrap_n = 200)
v2$ceiling$pairs
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   coder_a    coder_b    item         n agreement alpha
#>   <chr>      <chr>      <chr>    <int>     <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 annotator1 annotator2 category    20       0.6 0.704
v2$gap
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   item         n model_alpha coder_alpha     gap gap_ci       
#>   <chr>    <int>       <dbl>       <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>        
#> 1 category    20       0.669       0.704 -0.0352 [-0.39, 0.29]
